subject.title: feat(skills): declarative cron-trigger metadata in SKILL.md frontmatter

question: Should SKILL.md be allowed to declare scheduled or event triggers that OpenClaw registers autonomously, and what operator approval boundary must gate those triggers?
rationale: The source gap is real, but the requested behavior turns skill metadata into an autonomous execution source and crosses cron, hooks, plugin, ClawHub, and security ownership boundaries.

options.title: Define a gated trigger contract first
options.body: Keep this open until maintainers specify approved sources, consent, provenance, revocation, and whether implementation belongs in core skill metadata or a plugin API.

options.title: Limit to documentation metadata
options.body: Accept a non-executing trigger_description field for audits only, leaving actual scheduling in explicit cron jobs or plugins.

options.title: Keep scheduling outside skills
options.body: Reject autonomous SKILL.md scheduling and direct authors to explicit cron jobs, standing orders, hooks, or ClawHub plugins.

recommendation.title: Define a gated trigger contract first
recommendation.body: Keep this open until maintainers specify approved sources, consent, provenance, revocation, and whether implementation belongs in core skill metadata or a plugin API.

likelyOwner.reason: The unresolved part is the product/security contract, and recent history shows adjacent skills, docs, plugin, and cron policy work.
